sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface FLAG staining of VΔ3A2 by live-cell flow cytometry confirmed extracellular display, but surface expression required co-transduction of intact BTN3A molecules; VΔ3A2 alone did not traffic efficiently to the surface. Function is confounded by the presence of intact BTN3A co-expressed in the same cells.
sites.rationale: BTN3A2 is a type I single-pass transmembrane protein with a single extracellular N-terminus; after signal peptide cleavage (residues 1–29), the mature protein begins at Q30. The VΔ construct places FLAG at this sole extracellular terminus in a full-length membrane-anchored molecule, and live-cell flow cytometry confirms surface display. However, the entire V domain (approximately residues 30–130) is deleted rather than simply tagged, and surface expression requires co-expression of intact BTN3A molecules, indicating a trafficking defect in the absence of helper proteins. The position is topology-derived (no residue named in the paper); insert_after_residue=29 is the signal-peptide/mature-protein boundary confirmed from the canonical sequence (A29, Q30). Full-length, membrane-anchored BTN3A2 VΔ construct in which the entire V domain was replaced by a FLAG sequence preceded by a BTN3A1 leader sequence; expressed in transduced human cells and assessed by flow cytometry on live (surface) and permeabilized (total) cells. The FLAG tag is at the extracellular N-terminus of the construct, the only extracellular terminus of this type I single-pass protein. No specific residue junction is named; position is derived from the signal-peptide/mature-protein boundary (residue 29/30) of the canonical BTN3A2 sequence.

sources.claim: Cell surface FLAG-staining of VΔ3A2 also required co-transduction of intact 3A-molecules.

literature_notes: All five ledger lines (L1–L5) describe the same experimental system: a BTN3A2 VΔ construct in which the V domain is replaced by a FLAG tag preceded by a BTN3A1 leader sequence, expressed as a full-length membrane-anchored protein. L1 and L3 describe construct design; L2 and L4/L5 describe the flow cytometry readout. The critical finding in L2 is that surface FLAG staining of VΔ3A2 required co-transduction of intact BTN3A molecules, meaning the construct does not independently traffic to the surface. This co-expression requirement means validation_level is 'function_perturbed' rather than 'surface_only'. No ledger line names a specific residue junction; the position is topology-derived from the signal peptide boundary. The V domain deletion (approximately residues 30–130) is a substantial structural change beyond a simple short-tag insertion, further reducing confidence that a minimal ALFA-tag insertion at this junction would behave equivalently. No internal loop sites, C-terminal sites, or intracellular sites are described in any ledger line. No abrogating insertions are reported.
